summary: The graph is well grounded (all 384 condition quotes and 90 rule quotes are verbatim, all 26 Article 4 definitions are present, every Art 5-49 'shall' is mapped to a rule) and the rule inventory is a sound decomposition, but it is not yet safe as a coverage map. Two critical defects would generate wrong ALLOW outcomes: has_exception is used for facts that defeat a permission (no enforceable rights/remedies, BCR gaps, 49(3)/(5) limits), and thirteen rules that bind processors in the text obligate only the controller. Major accuracy errors include Art 23 overriding security/minimisation principles it cannot touch, an inconsistent Art 89 derogation map, Art 22(3) safeguards imposed on law-authorised decisions, a processor-receipt 'exception' to the access right, Art 6(3) modelled as an exception, and Art 10 labelled overlay while Art 9 is core. Completeness gaps: no Chapter I scope layer (Arts 2-3), no Art 9 -> Art 6 dependency (Recital 51), the right to withdraw consent is given effect by no rule, and 41 conditions (10% of the layer, including the 22(4) safeguard, 49(1)(a) risk information and 36(3) package) are isolated. Modelling choices that make coverage counting misleading: exceptions are stored two or three times across base and exception rules, 14 pairs of near-duplicate conditions survive the merge, node-level polarity disagrees with edge usage on 37 edges, there is no way to express conjunctive conditions or which trigger an exception qualifies, and depends_on contains four cycles. Hygiene: actions, roles and deadlines carry no grounding despite the documentation's claim, 35 references use ids that do not resolve to structure.json, and the 72-hour / one-month deadline nodes have no provenance. All findings carry mechanical fixes; applying F001-F010 and the duplicate-merge, conjunction and polarity schema changes (F016-F020) should be done before the graph is used to plan scenario coverage.

findings.target: CS-09 (scope=overlay) vs CS-07 (scope=core); CS-08 (scope=overlay)
findings.problem: Scope labels are inconsistent for structurally identical rules. Art 10, like Art 9, is a GDPR default prohibition whose exceptions depend on law: an agent for a private controller must DENY criminal-offence processing unless an official-authority or statutory ground is supplied. Labelling the whole rule "overlay" (while CS-07 is "core") risks the generator skipping Art 10 scenarios and makes core/overlay coverage counts wrong. Overlay status belongs on the exception conditions (as CS-07 does), not the rule.
